The view asks the forge once per repository: gh pr list --state all --limit 100 (glab mr list --all --per-page 100) run in the repository the agent's tree was cut from, and each branch's requests are cut out of that answer by head name. A pr-<N> branch (new --pr on a fork's request, or a taken name) is matched to request N by number, which the old per-branch --head ask never found. A branch a full answer of 100 leaves out is asked about alone with --head; a pr-<N> branch is not, since by name it would read as having no request. sweep's asked_now stays per branch. The schedule is in memory per repository in t3; t4 moves it to disk

# plan: quiet-waits

- [x] t1 result and wait read the phase without capturing a pane for the spinner line
- [x] t2 Pin one listing and one capture call per server for a reading, and one listing for ls
- [x] t3 The view asks the forge once per repository and matches each branch from that answer
- [ ] t4 A failing forge is asked at doubling gaps up to 16 minutes, and an ended agent with no request every 10 minutes  [after: t3]
